scope: 158 captured RSS articles, 2 days, 2 fresh rebuild replays; saved old assignments, no latest-legacy rerun
label_scope: Selected independent-agent judgments, not representative accuracy or human gold; disputed legacy positives kept separate

input_manifest.evidence: captured title plus HTML-stripped RSS description; bodies excluded
input_manifest.order: chronological days, original snapshot order, greedy bounded batches

source_review_summary.recommended_primary_subset: The seven negative cases support a narrow false-merge check only. There are no independently confirmed positive exact-event edges in these ten RSS-only cases under the strict policy, so this subset cannot estimate recall or balanced event-matching accuracy.
source_review_summary.comparison_reporting: Keep original legacy labels visible for historical compatibility, but separate those proxy scores from evidence-supported correctness. Do not relabel the three uncertain positives as proven negatives after observing system outputs.

legacy_labels.review_note: Different clubs and transfer developments must not share one event memory.
A transfer roundup and an unrelated friendly/injury item are separate events.
The Lipowitz crash and unrelated timing commentary are not one concrete event.
A retailer drone strike and military-chief appointment are separate developments.
The current analysis directly continues France's under-15 social-media restriction; all listed candidates are duplicate reports of that restriction.
Both concern the same named youth protest movement in India; either reviewed day-one report is an acceptable continuation target.
The apology is a direct follow-up to the same World Cup final incident.
A player becoming unwell and a different match result are distinct stories inside the World Matchplay tournament arc.
A tram collision is not the same event as national bridge inspections.
Generic tax overlap does not establish the same concrete story.

excluded_legacy_cases.reason: The saved Trouw occurrence has a question-style headline but no description or body text, so the shared incident cannot be established from retained source evidence.

additional_positive_labels.review_note: RTL and NOS identify the same French parliamentary approval of an under-15 social-media restriction, with France described as the first EU country to adopt it and September implementation intended. This is a particular legislative decision, not just discussion of youth phone use.

NOS and BBC both explicitly identify Zelensky dismissing army commander Oleksandr Syrsky/Syrskyi after protests related to Defense Minister Fedorov being removed. The named dismissed officer, decision maker and immediate context match. This is the same dismissal, not generic Ukraine-war coverage.

The Telegraaf and RTL descriptions identify Fred and Ceciel separating after their first night or within 24 hours, resulting in the first exit from this B&B Vol Liefde season. They describe the same pair and specific departure. Sharing a recurring television format would not alone be enough.

The Telegraaf description explicitly reports Trump receiving Lebanese president Joseph Aoun at the White House for talks involving Hezbollah, Israeli withdrawal and Lebanese security. The Washington Post title and description report Trump meeting his Lebanese counterpart and pledging support for restoring government control in the same southern territory. The same-day presidential meeting is the common occurrence; the joke and pledge are aspects of it.

NOS and NYT both report thousands returning to demonstrate in New Delhi one day after police violently dispersed protesters, with education grievances motivating the action. These shared location, timing and occurrence details identify the renewed demonstration. NOS adds Gandhi being taken away; the match is established by the concrete renewed protest, not merely by a shared movement label.

RTL and NOS describe Trump approving the same civil nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia, enabling domestic nuclear facilities and leaving open possible uranium enrichment. Both retain this distinctive approval and provision. This supports one agreement decision, without claiming enrichment has already begun.

NOS and NU.nl identify Ali B withdrawing from the upcoming speaking engagement at The Harbour Club in Vinkeveen after criticism of the booking. The named speaker, venue, town and withdrawal match. This is the withdrawal event, not a general match to all coverage of his court case.

NU.nl and NOS report release of the 18-year-old Rotterdam man initially detained over the fatal Nijmegen shooting, and both state he is no longer a suspect. The specific suspect status change, location and person details align; neither RSS suggests two different releases.

NU.nl and Guardian both identify Nicaragua legislature moving to implement Daniel Ortega's order to stop holding elections. Guardian explicitly calls the announced implementation a work plan; NU.nl describes parliament putting the same plan into effect. The match is the legislative implementation development, not every report about Nicaraguan repression.

NU.nl and Telegraaf both name Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala apologizing for his altercation with Spain's Dani Olmo after the World Cup final. Both the specific actors and the apology development are explicit. This differs from the disputed prior BBC excerpt that only referenced general ugly scenes and a different person defending the team.

The July 21 NOS description names Rahul Gandhi being taken away by police during the renewed Indian protests. The next-day Al Jazeera title reports Gandhi speaking after release, and its description calls this his first public statement since arrest during protests. The named person and explicit arrest-to-release sequence establish a direct follow-up, unlike a generic explainer about the protest movement.

The earlier Washington Post RSS names Hegseth and Caine appearing before the Senate while lawmakers seek clarity on a $67 billion Iran-war funding request. The next update names Hegseth defending additional funding and reports lawmakers expressing frustration over that same $67 billion request. This is a hearing progression from anticipated questioning to remarks and reaction. The source article identifier and URL are also unchanged, but the shared hearing/funding details, not identifier equality alone, support the event link.

positive_label_caveats: These are independent-agent judgments, not human-reviewed ground truth or verified facts about the reported news.

They assess concrete occurrence identity or a direct reported development. They do not automatically merge articles merely because they share a movement, war, tournament, recurring program, actor or URL.
This is a deliberately selected positive audit, not a random or exhaustive benchmark. Results cannot establish corpus-wide precision, recall, balanced accuracy or real-world generalization.

The two cross-day pairs are supported by explicit arrest/release progression and hearing/funding-request details. The Hegseth pair is an update to one source article, so it is not independent corroboration from two publishers.

The positive same-day India pair concerns a concrete renewed New Delhi demonstration; the cross-day Gandhi pair concerns the arrest/release sequence. Both share one prior article and are not independent statistical samples.
Titles and RSS descriptions are the complete permitted semantic evidence for this audit. Long NOS descriptions are still frozen RSS fields; scraped full-body text was not used.
The original ten legacy labels and the frozen source-review.json remain unchanged. Additional positives must be reported separately from that historical compatibility set.
